## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nikkaḍḍhana-sikkhāpada* ("Evicting a nun", Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 35) is a monastic disciplinary rule found in the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. According to the rule, a nun who assigns or gives a dwelling place to another nun and later drives her out or throws her out commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. In modern examinations of monastic organization, this rule is noted as the bhikkhunī counterpart to Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 17, both of which penalize monastics who evict fellow community members from monastery lodgings [Wijayaratna 1990]. An English translation of the text is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this rule was preserved across the Vinayas of multiple Buddhist schools, including the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 94*), Mahīśāsaka (*Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc167*), Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc86*), Mūlasarvāstivāda (*xct-mu-bi-vb-pc153*), Mahāsāṅghika (*Lzh Mg Bi Vb Pc136*), and Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda (*san-lo-bi-vb-pc136*) traditions [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse data from DharmaNexus reflects this correspondence, indicating that the text shares its largest Pali-internal parallel with the male counterpart rule Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 17 (§2.1.11–2.2.7 ↔ §2.1.6–2.2.7), alongside shared phrasing with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 33 [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus establishes automated cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005), aligning with the Mūlasarvāstivāda parallel identified by SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
